sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **The Caliphate (Khilafat)**: The Ottoman Sultan was considered the **Khalifa** (spiritual head of Muslims worldwide). The Treaty of Sèvres (1920) dismantled the Ottoman Empire, sparking outrage.
• **The Khilafat Committee**: Formed in March 1919 in Bombay by the **Ali Brothers** (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali), Hasrat Mohani, and Maulana Azad.
• **The Alliance**: Gandhi saw this as an 'opportunity of a lifetime' to unite Hindus and Muslims against British rule, leading to the merger of Khilafat and Non-Cooperation agendas.
• **Key Metric**: The movement transitioned from a religious grievance to a broader anti-colonial struggle, peaking between 1920-1922.

items.definition: The post-WWI treaty that imposed harsh terms on the Ottoman Empire, serving as the immediate trigger for the movement.
Held in Delhi (Nov 1919), where Gandhi was elected president, signaling the formal integration of the Khilafat cause with the Indian National Congress.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Non-Cooperation**: Adoption of the four-stage program: boycott of titles, civil services, courts, and foreign goods.
• **Hijrat Movement**: A radical offshoot where thousands of Indian Muslims migrated to Afghanistan, viewing India as 'Dar-ul-Harb' (land of war).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: The movement collapsed in 1924 when Mustafa Kemal Atatürk abolished the Caliphate in Turkey.
• **Solutions**: The movement left a legacy of mass mobilization techniques that were later refined in the Civil Disobedience Movement.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-A-M-A' (Khilafat, Ali Brothers, Maulana Azad, All India Committee).
• **Decoded Meaning**: K (Khilafat), A (Ali Brothers), M (Maulana Azad), A (All India Committee).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The Khilafat Movement was NOT a purely religious movement; it was a political movement with religious symbolism used to mobilize the masses against British imperialism.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Syncretic Nationalism' to describe the alliance between the Khilafat movement and the Indian National Congress.

keyTakeaways: The movement was triggered by the harsh terms of the Treaty of Sèvres.
Gandhi's support was pivotal in merging the Khilafat issue with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
The movement ended abruptly due to the secularization of Turkey under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
